patch.title: Aramis Battery: 100 MW EIA Rating; County Approval in March 2021
patch.description: Alameda County’s filed Notice of Determination records March 4, 2021 approval of the 347-acre Resource Management Avoidance Alternative for Aramis. EIA plant 66678 separately reports 100 MW solar and 100 MW battery, under construction at no more than 50% completion in August 2026.

patch.longFormSummary:
• The county applicant is IP Aramis LLC, an Intersect Power subsidiary. The filed March 2021 determination controls the approval milestone; earlier November 2020 pages in the packet are not the latest approval. The 2020 EIR alternative diagram labels 385 acres and is historical, not the final approved 347-acre footprint.
  • EIA’s September 2026 and CAISO’s July 31, 2026 targets have passed without opened proof of actual COD. CAISO lists 101.4 MW solar, 101.3 MW storage and 100 MW combined export at Cayetano 230 kV. Native 100 MW represents EIA battery only; the EIR four-hour design objective is not an explicit verified 400 MWh installed rating. Removed $140M and invented April 2027 COD.
  • Timeline: Confirmed March 4, 2021 county approval in the filed Notice of Determination. This is not a COD; queue and EIA operating targets are unverified.

The March 2021 approval describes a 347-acre alternative; this diagram is not an as-built boundary or construction photograph. Credit: HELIX Environmental Planning / Alameda County; underlying DigitalGlobe 2018 imagery as shown.

patch.title: Arkansas Cypress: 350 MW Battery Under Construction, 2029 Target
patch.description: Entergy’s October 19, 2026 release explicitly says Arkansas Cypress Solar and Battery is under construction in Jefferson County. Its current October-2026 portfolio lists 600 MW solar and 350 MW battery targeting 2029; EIA plant 69989 reports January 2029 planned operation.

references.title: Entergy Renewable Energy — Arkansas Cypress, as of October 2026
EIA August 2026 Inventory — Arkansas Cypress Solar Station 69989
Entergy Arkansas announces enhanced partnership at Google West Memphis campus, delivering at least $500M in new savings for all customers

patch.longFormSummary:
• The current opened operator table says 2029, superseding stale search snippets that still say 2028. EIA’s August approvals-not-initiated code is a dated inventory report, not a current finding that no application exists. Native capacity is battery-only 350 MW; the shared 1,659 MW interconnection includes a separate 730 MW combined-cycle plant and is not battery or solar capacity.
  • No opened support for the former $420M, 1,400 MWh, four-hour rating or November 2028 COD. Exact battery footprint and current approval remain research gaps.
  • Timeline: January 1 is month-only precision for EIA January 2029; current operator says year 2029. Neither is an exact confirmed operating day.
  • The October 19 operator construction statement supersedes EIA’s dated August approvals-not-initiated status. New Driver and Jones Mill batteries and their combined 2,800 MWh program total are not assigned to Cypress as a standalone battery energy rating.

researchNotes: Ten existing pins corrected and two duplicate identities soft-deleted/held on local and production. Preserved original authors, reconciled stale local IDs against live title/source/author snapshots, re-read records immediately before each write and retained backups. No new pins, automatic merges or deployment.

Read August 2026 EIA, September 2026 ERCOT GIS and CAISO primary workbooks. Generator MW, battery energy, combined export and campus electrical service are separate scopes. Proposed operating dates do not prove actual operation; date precision and milestone type are explicit in each saved record.

Amerada: EIA 67649 supports 300 MW solar, Cypress Creek Renewables, approvals pending and July 2029. ERCOT 26INR0082 instead gives 301.57 MW / December 30, 2028 with screening complete, study started and no IA. Separate Amerada Storage is not added. No project-specific operator gallery or precise parcel found in current searches.

Aramis: visually read the scanned county Notice of Determination. The March 4, 2021 approval of a 347-acre Resource Management Avoidance Alternative controls; March 10 is the county filing stamp and the packet also includes superseded November 2020 material. EIA 66678 supports 100 MW battery and separate 100 MW solar, no more than 50% construction complete in August 2026. EIA September and CAISO July 31, 2026 targets have passed without COD proof. CAISO reports 101.3 MW storage / 101.4 MW solar / 100 MW export. EIR four-hour design objective is not promoted to an explicit installed 400 MWh rating. The historical EIR Figure 5-1 labels 385 acres, distinguished from the later 347-acre approval.

Arida 16695 held as duplicate of corrected 16615: same EIA 63841 370 MW battery, same coordinates and CAISO 1522 hybrid. Verified the retained pin on both environments before holding the redundant identity; no independent second battery phase or cancellation inferred.

Arkansas Cypress: opened October-2026 operator table says 600 MW solar / 350 MW battery, Jefferson County and 2029 target, superseding stale 2028 search snippets. October 19 company release explicitly says under construction, superseding EIA August approvals-not-initiated coding. The 1,659 MW shared POI includes separate 730 MW CCCT. New Driver/Jones Mill battery additions and combined 2,800 MWh program total are not a standalone Cypress energy rating. No battery-only cost inferred from whole-project spending or Google customer payments. Current standalone MWh remains a gap.

Atlas IV: current TransGrid project page verifies under construction, 150 MW / 600 MWh, mid-2027 target; EIA 68321 instead gives March 2027 and over 50% complete. Solar 300 MW / Q4-2026 is a separate PV project. Both operator BESS and overall PV/BESS construction images are credited with scope qualifications. The company resolver returned an unrelated Hanwha Group Wikipedia URL for TransGrid Energy, so company uses exact EIA legal project entity ATLAS BESS IV LLC while operator attribution remains in text; no shared company metadata edited.

ORD-02: downloaded the October 15, 2024 working operator sheet: 36 MW critical, 228,768 gross sqft, 501 Northwest Avenue. Shared Northlake campus is 18.5 acres; ORD-01 at 505 is separate. April 19, 2022 is the second-building groundbreaking announcement, not a verified COD or the later specification date. Campus 72 MW / 170 MW substation service is not building IT load. Seven exact-building gallery photos inspected.

DFW-02: September 13, 2022 primary announcement specifies 36 MW critical, 220,000 gross sqft including 185,000 data hall; 19 acres is shared campus. Later operator blog confirms grand opening and new headquarters but no exact event day adopted. Four exact-building interior gallery photos and four opening-blog images inspected and credited. No modeled 50.4 MW, $1.36B or fabricated March-2027 COD retained.

IAD01: September 16, 2019 primary release states 12 MW built out in 368,755 gross sqft, expandable to 60 MW, with formal commissioning under way. Native 60 MW is explicitly expansion/design scope, not initial energized load. Downloaded case study introduction/named IAD01 summary agree with 60 MW, but one results paragraph says 80 MW; record that internal conflict. The separate 120 MW IAD02 and shared 26-acre campus are not IAD01-only scope. Current exact operator address 21890 Uunet Drive replaces wrong Smith Switch Road address. Six exact-building gallery images inspected.

NEO-01: September 25, 2023 acquisition announcement supports 129-acre Perkins Township brownfield planned four-building campus, NEO-01 first. Current address is 2509 Hayes Avenue. No building-specific support for 82.8 MW, old floor area, $2.73B or May-2027 COD: native power removed. Case-study projected 99% water/discharge reduction compares with former industrial operations, not metered daily water or all other data centers. Current exterior case-study image retained; generic Ohio-map release hero rejected. Older water-study PDF inaccessible.

Adamstown 16730 held as duplicate of 16681: downloaded January 2, 2025 PUCT filing explicitly names Adams Creek Solar Project, LLC (Adamstown Solar), request 21INR0210. Retained Adams Creek pin already represents EIA 70300 / 250 MW and 2027 target. ERCOT 250.88 MW / August 31, 2027 is queue precision, not evidence of an additional project. Both retained-pin identities verified unchanged; no automatic merge.

Waiawa Phase 2: operator states August 21, 2023 construction start, 30 MWac solar / 240 MWh battery, up to 387 acres and two 46 kV circuit interconnections. Distinct from operating 36 MW Waiawa Solar Power. Native 30 MW is solar alone. July-2026 schedule targets operation in 2026, while August EIA reports September target / construction over 50%; neither establishes actual operation by the research date. Three operator diagrams retained (March/April 2021 proposed maps and July-2026 schedule); unverified header ceremony photograph excluded.

Antila: ERCOT 27INR0500 supports legal applicant Antila Solar LLC, 500 MW, Borden County, Buck Canyon 345 kV and November 30, 2027 projected COD. WETT public notice published February 3, 2026 in Lamesa Press-Reporter identifies SE DC DevCo as developer of Juno Solar 3 and Antila totaling approximately 1 GW, and proposed collector stations east-northeast of FM 1054 N / US 180. It is primary published notice text, not an independent estimate. Its $84.3M transmission budget is not Antila solar capex. Ultimate parent and current PUCT 59199 outcome remain gaps; no unsupported SB Energy tag or acreage retained. Do not trust secondary tracker operational classification of a future queue date.

Cleared ten unsupported prices and four calculated energy rows per environment. Replaced all four datacenter metric rows to clear unverified daily water, hardware and generator assertions. Ratings remain historical/design scope rather than derived actual consumption.
